Key growth platforms are also doing what the thesis requires. World Financial Group lifted life sales 5% and annuity sales 12%, with more producers active and higher average premiums. Retirement plans saw solid written sales and a 10 basis point uplift in return on assets, even though one large contract termination pulled net deposits into negative territory. Bears also focus on model and assumption sensitivity. The annual review produced a €231m after tax hit from policyholder behavior changes, mainly in U.S. variable annuities and life premium patterns. Berkshire trades on a P/E of 12.4x, which is well below the diversified financial industry average of 17.4x and the broader peer average of 23.2x. That already points to the stock changing hands at a lower price for each dollar of recent earnings than many comparable companies.

The fair P/E ratio from Simply Wall St’s model is 16.5x. This reflects what investors might typically pay for a business with Berkshire Hathaway’s size, margins and risk profile. Set against the current 12.4x, Berkshire shares trade at a sizeable discount to this tailored benchmark. Recent portfolio shifts into housing and Alphabet have not removed that gap, so the current earnings multiple still prices Berkshire below what the model suggests is reasonable.

On the P/E multiple, Berkshire Hathaway stock appears undervalued relative to both its industry peers and the model’s fair ratio.
